rationale: JPA @Entity mapped to the 'owners' table, with validated fields and a one-to-many Pet association. An ORM entity class is a data-model ObjectSchema that maps to the owners collection. It is a core domain entity of petclinic, but it performs no storage I/O itself, so data_persistence is false.

HTTP POST /owners/new route handler is an API operation contract: it validates the Owner form, persists the owner via the repository, and drives the server-rendered UI by returning a view or a redirect with flash messages.

Spring Data repository interface defining read operations (findAll, paged findAll) against the vets table with caching; it is the persistence access layer for Vet entities. Its query methods are data-store access patterns, and it is a significant store integration point.

A Spring @Configuration class that wires the application's i18n support: a session-based locale resolver and a URL-parameter locale-change interceptor. It is a notable configuration component a maintainer would name when explaining localisation, not core architecture. It drives user-facing language selection; session storage is in-memory, so it is not durable persistence.

Spring @InitBinder boilerplate that stops request binding from setting 'id' fields, a small mass-assignment guard. It is a framework configuration hook inside the controller, below the level a maintainer would name as an architectural element, so it is not modelled as a node.

Trivial getter on the Pet entity returning a field. Accessors are implementation details below modelling granularity; the birthDate property itself would be modelled as a schema property of the Pet object schema, not this method.

Spring Data JPA repository for PetType with a custom JPQL query that orders by name. It is repository/DAO code issuing reads against the pet types table, so it is best modelled as a data-store access pattern. It is a small but notable persistence unit.

HTTP GET route /owners/{ownerId}/edit handled by OwnerController. It is a distinct method-path endpoint, so it is modelled as an API operation. It returns a server-rendered form view name, so it drives the UI. It has no logic of its own beyond view selection, which makes it a notable but not central endpoint.

A Spring @Component Formatter that converts between form text and PetType, looking up types through the injected repository. It is MVC binding glue, a minor dependency-injected component rather than a service. It does no persistence itself; it delegates the lookup to the repository.

HTTP GET route /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/edit bound to a Spring MVC handler; one method-path pair is an API operation. It returns the pet create/update form view name, so it drives a server-rendered UI. It is a notable but ordinary endpoint in the PetClinic owner module.

A Spring Data JPA repository for Owner entities. It declares the query methods the application issues against the owners table: a paginated last-name prefix search and a lookup by id. Repository code that talks to storage belongs in the data-store layer, and its derived queries are access patterns. It is the central persistence integration point for the owner module.

Spring Boot application entry point that bootstraps the whole PetClinic application. It is the root deployable application component and the system's main entry point, so it is a core architectural element. It implements no cross-cutting concern directly.

Spring MVC handler bound to GET /owners/find, so it is one method-path HTTP operation of the server-side surface. It only returns the 'owners/findOwners' view name, serving the search form page, which is a user-interface concern. The logic is trivial, so significance is moderate.

Boilerplate override of Spring's Validator.supports that only checks whether a class is assignable to Pet. This is a framework type-check accessor with no behaviour of its own. It is an implementation detail of PetValidator, not an architectural element.

An HTTP GET route on /owners/{ownerId} is an API operation contract (one method on one path template). It serves the owner details page, so it drives the UI via a server-rendered view. Persistence is delegated to the repository rather than performed here. It is a significant entry point into the owner domain.

Vets is a JAXB-annotated wrapper type whose shape is published as the XML/JSON response payload of the /vets resource endpoint. It is a serialized, schema-published structure rather than an internal carrier, so it fits data-model objectschema. It is a minor but nameable element with no behaviour.

A private helper inside VetController that builds a Pageable and delegates to VetRepository.findAll. This is pagination plumbing below the level a maintainer would model. Persistence is done by the repository, not by this method.

An HTTP GET route on /owners/find is a distinct method-path endpoint, so it is modelled as an API operation. Its handler only returns the findOwners view name, which makes it a server-rendered page entry. It is a simple endpoint of moderate significance, and it drives the UI by selecting the template to render.

Spring MVC handler bound to GET /owners. It is an HTTP operation contract that searches owners by last name with pagination, then selects a view or redirect. Persistence goes through a helper, not this method. It drives the web UI by choosing and populating view templates.

Spring MVC controller exposing GET /oups, which deliberately throws an exception to showcase error-page handling. It is an HTTP route handler, so it belongs to the api layer as a single operation. It is a demo endpoint of minor architectural weight with no business logic.

HTTP GET /vets route returning a JSON/XML Vets resource via @ResponseBody. This is an API operation contract (one method on one path) in Spring PetClinic. It reads through the repository but does not itself implement persistence.

Private helper in OwnerController that builds a Pageable and delegates to the repository query. It is an implementation detail of processFindForm, not an architectural element. It calls the persistence layer but does not itself perform storage access.

JPA @Entity mapped to the 'vets' table, with a many-to-many specialties association. It is a core domain entity of the petclinic model. Per the charter, an ORM entity class is an objectschema that specializes Person and maps to the data-store collection. It holds state rather than performing persistence I/O itself, so no concern applies.

GraalVM native-image runtime hints registrar: framework build/boilerplate configuration that registers resource patterns and reflection types. It is not an architecturally meaningful element on its own. At most it is a minor technology-related detail, so it is classified as scaffolding with low significance.

Private helper that builds a JCache MutableConfiguration with statistics enabled. It is an implementation detail of the CacheConfiguration class, used only by the cache customizer, and is below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element.

A server-side HTTP GET / endpoint in Spring MVC. Server endpoints belong to the api layer rather than navigation, so it is modelled as an api operation. It only returns the 'welcome' Thymeleaf view name, so it drives the web UI's landing page. It is a simple but recognisable entry point.

HTTP GET /owners route handler in a Spring MVC controller: a method-path contract, so it is an API operation. It searches owners by last name and paginates the results, choosing a server-rendered view or redirect, so it drives the UI. Persistence is delegated to the repository via a helper.

HTTP GET /vets handler returning a @ResponseBody Vets payload (JSON/XML resource endpoint). It is a route handler bound to one method-path pair, so it is an API operation. It reads via the repository but does not itself implement persistence.

Pet is a JPA @Entity mapped to the pets table, a core domain entity with relationships to PetType and Visit. Per the spec, an ORM entity class is a data-model objectschema that maps to a data-store collection. It only declares the mapping and does no storage I/O itself, so data_persistence is false.

An HTTP GET route bound to one method-path pair (/owners/{ownerId}/pets/new) is an API operation. It is a server-rendered MVC endpoint that prepares a new Pet and returns the create/update form view, so it drives the UI. Significance is moderate: a single CRUD form endpoint in the sample app.

Spring Validator registered by PetController's binder to check Pet form input (name required and at most 30 chars, type for new pets, birth date required). This is internal application-side validation behaviour serving the owner/pet component, not a security access decision or engine-enforced constraint. It is a notable unit a maintainer would name.

An HTTP GET /oups route handler is an API operation, but it exists only to demonstrate error handling by throwing an exception. It is a demo endpoint with no business behaviour, so its architectural significance is low.

Spring Data repository query method that reads paginated Vet records from the store, cached under 'vets'. It is a named read operation issued by application code against the vets collection, i.e. a data-store access pattern. It is notable within the repository but is a single query rather than a component.

Constructor of VisitController that only assigns the injected OwnerRepository dependency. This is dependency-injection boilerplate with no behaviour of its own. The controller class may be architecturally meaningful, but its constructor is not an element in its own right.

JPA @MappedSuperclass that defines the generated identity property shared by all petclinic entities. It is an ORM entity base class, so it is a data-model object schema that the concrete entities specialize. It is a notable but small shared abstraction and performs no storage I/O itself.

This is an HTTP POST route, one method on one path, that handles the pet edit form submission. It validates the input, updates the pet and either redirects or re-renders the form. It is an API operation contract at the system boundary. The user_interface flag is set because the handler drives the MVC form views; persistence is delegated to updatePetDetails.

An HTTP POST route binding a method plus path to a form-submission handler is an API operation. It validates the visit, persists it through the owner repository, and drives the MVC UI by returning a view name, a redirect and a flash message. It is a significant endpoint in the visit-booking flow.

A Spring configuration class that enables caching and creates the JCache 'vets' cache with statistics exposed via JMX. It is infrastructure set-up rather than application logic, so it is best modelled as the caching technology service the application relies on. Its significance is moderate.

JPA @Entity mapped to the 'specialties' table, extending NamedEntity. It is an ORM domain entity describing a vet's specialty, so it is a data-model object schema that specializes NamedEntity and maps to a data-store collection. It is a small but nameable domain entity and performs no I/O itself.

Spring Data derived query method on OwnerRepository: a named read operation against the owners table, filtered by last-name prefix with pagination. That matches a data-store access pattern issued from application code. It is notable as the owner search query used by OwnerController.

Spring MVC controller class exposing the vet list as both an HTML view and a JSON resource. As a mounted controller it is the access point to vet listing behaviour, so it is an application interface. It drives UI rendering via the model and view name, while persistence is delegated to VetRepository.

A Spring @Bean that registers the JCache 'vets' cache with the cache manager. It is platform caching configuration rather than business logic, so it belongs to the technology layer. As a one-line wiring method it carries little significance on its own; the caching capability is better modelled at the CacheConfiguration level.

HTTP GET /owners/new route handled by the Spring MVC OwnerController. It is one method-path pair, so it is an api operation. It returns the owner create/update form view, so it drives the UI. It is a simple form-initialization endpoint of moderate significance.

This is a Spring AOT/GraalVM native-image runtime hints registration method. It declares resource patterns and reflection types for native compilation. It is framework boilerplate and build configuration rather than an architectural element. At most it is a minor technology detail that a maintainer would not name when explaining the system.

JPA @MappedSuperclass entity base defining firstName/lastName with column and validation constraints; an ORM model is an object schema. It is an abstract base specialized by Owner and Vet, so it is notable but not core. It only declares mapping annotations and performs no storage I/O itself.

HTTP POST route handler for /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/new. It is a distinct method-path contract, so it is modelled as an API operation. It validates the visit date, saves the owner through the repository, and drives the MVC form view and redirect, so it covers data persistence and the user interface.

An HTTP POST route handler for /owners/{ownerId}/pets/new is one method-path pair, so it is an api operation. It validates the submitted pet, saves the owner through the repository, and returns or redirects to an MVC form view. It is a significant system boundary for the pet creation feature.

HTTP GET route bound to a distinct method-path pair in a Spring MVC controller, so it is an API operation. It returns the view name for the new-visit form, which means it drives server-rendered UI. As a system-boundary endpoint it is architecturally significant.

A Spring MVC @Controller mounted at /owners/{ownerId}. It is the HTTP access point for the pet create and edit web forms: it handles requests, validates input, renders Thymeleaf views and saves owners through the repository. The individual route methods would be API operations; the controller class as a whole is an application interface.

JPA @MappedSuperclass that adds a validated name column to BaseEntity and serves as an abstract base for PetType, Specialty and others. It is an ORM model shape, so it is modelled as a data-model object schema that subclasses specialize. It is a shared base rather than a core entity, and it does no storage I/O itself.

A Spring MVC handler bound to GET /, so it is modelled as an HTTP operation. It returns the 'welcome' view name, rendering the server-side home page, which makes the user_interface concern true. It is the application's landing entry, but it has no logic, so significance is moderate.

Spring MVC POST handler for /owners/{ownerId}/pets/new: an HTTP method-path contract, so it is an API operation. It validates the pet, persists it through the owner repository (saveAndFlush), and drives the UI by returning the form view or redirecting with a flash message.

A JPA @Entity mapped to the 'visits' table and extending BaseEntity is a core domain entity. Per the data-model rules, an ORM entity class is an object schema, which maps to the data-store collection. Its persistence mapping annotations justify data_persistence.

A trivial setter on the Visit entity. Accessors are implementation details below the granularity of an architectural element. The Visit entity itself would be the data-model object schema, and its description field would be a schema property, but this method is neither.

A Spring @Bean factory method that configures the framework's LocaleChangeInterceptor with a 'lang' URL parameter. This is configuration boilerplate inside WebConfiguration, not an element a maintainer would name on its own. At most it is an attribute of the i18n configuration.

JPA @Entity mapped to the 'types' table, extending NamedEntity. An ORM entity class is an object schema in the data-model layer. It is a small lookup entity (Cat, Dog, ...) with no behaviour, but it is a domain type a maintainer would name. It maps to the data-store collection rather than performing persistence itself.

A trivial setter on the NamedEntity base class. Accessors are implementation details below model granularity. At most, the owning entity would be modelled as a data-model object schema with a 'name' property; the setter itself is not an element. It performs no persistence, I/O or other cross-cutting work.

A Spring @Bean factory method that wires a session-based locale resolver with an English default. This is framework configuration boilerplate for i18n, below the granularity of an architectural element. At most it is part of the WebConfiguration component.

A Spring MVC controller whose only member is the GET / route handler, which returns the 'welcome' template name. It is best modelled as one HTTP operation (GET /) serving the home page. It is a trivial landing endpoint, notable but not core. It does drive the web UI by selecting the view to render.

Trivial getter on the Person entity returning a field. Accessors fall below the model's granularity; the lastName property would be modelled as a schema property of the Person object schema, not as this method.

A Spring MVC controller is the access point for visit-booking behaviour. It binds GET and POST routes, validates form input and returns server-rendered views with flash messages. As a whole controller it fits ApplicationInterface; its individual routes would be api operations. Persistence is delegated to OwnerRepository, so data_persistence is false.

Spring @InitBinder framework hook that wires PetValidator into the controller's data binder and disallows binding of id fields. It is controller configuration boilerplate. Validation and mass-assignment protection matter, but at the level of PetValidator and the controller, not this method, so it is below model granularity.

Spring MVC GET handler bound to /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/edit; one method-path pair is an API operation. It returns the pet create/update form view name, driving the UI. It is a thin handler, so it is a notable but not central element.

A @ModelAttribute pre-handler inside VisitController. It loads the owner through the repository, then prepares the pet and a new Visit for the model. This is internal controller plumbing, not a route or contract of its own. It is a minor application function, and it reaches persistence only by calling the repository.

A boilerplate toString override on the Owner entity. It only formats field values into a string for debugging. It is an implementation detail with no architectural meaning of its own, so it would not be recorded as an element in the model.

Trivial JavaBean accessor on the Person entity that just returns a field. Accessors are excluded by the granularity rule; the firstName property would be modelled as a schemaproperty of the Person object schema, not this getter method.

Trivial JavaBean setter on the Person entity, which only assigns a field. Accessors are implementation details, not architectural elements. Person itself would be a data-model object schema, but this method has no architectural meaning of its own.

Constructor of the Visit entity that only defaults the date to tomorrow. It is an implementation detail of the entity class, which would itself be the data-model object schema. A constructor is not an architectural element on its own.

Private helper in VetController that only populates Spring MVC model attributes for pagination and returns the view name. It is an implementation detail of the showVetList handler, below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element.

Trivial setter on the Person entity. Accessors are implementation details below modelling granularity. The lastName field may be a schema property of the Person object schema, but the setter itself is not an architectural element.

Trivial getter on the Owner entity that returns a field. Accessors are implementation details and are not architectural elements. The city attribute would at most be modelled as a schema property of the Owner object schema, not as this method.

A trivial derived accessor on the Vet entity that returns the size of the specialties collection. It is an implementation detail below the granularity of an architecture element; the Vet entity itself would be the modelled data-model object schema.

Trivial setter on the Owner entity that only assigns a field. Accessors are implementation details, not architectural elements. The Owner entity itself would be a data-model object schema, but this method has no architectural significance on its own.

A trivial setter on the Owner entity. It only assigns a field and has no logic. Accessors are implementation details below modelling granularity. The city field could be a schemaproperty of the Owner object schema, but the setter itself is not an element.

A trivial collection mutator on the Pet JPA entity that appends a Visit to its in-memory visits list. It is an accessor-level implementation detail of the entity, not an architectural element. Persistence happens elsewhere, through the repository save.

Trivial accessor on the Visit entity returning a field. Accessors are implementation details below the granularity of architectural elements; the Visit entity itself would be the modelled data-model element, not its getter.

An accessor on the Vet entity that returns specialties sorted by name, annotated for XML serialization. It is a trivial getter and an implementation detail of the Vet object schema, not an architectural element on its own.

Spring Formatter method that converts a form string to a PetType by looking it up through the repository. It is a conversion helper below architectural granularity. Persistence is reached only through the called repository, so this method does no persistence work itself.

Collection-mutator method on the Owner entity that adds a pet while avoiding duplicates. It is an entity accessor-level helper, below the granularity of an architectural element. The Owner object schema is the element; this method itself performs no persistence.

Spring MVC configuration boilerplate: a framework-callback override that only registers the locale change interceptor with the registry. It is wiring scaffolding below the granularity of an architectural element and implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

Constructor that only stores an injected PetTypeRepository dependency. It is trivial dependency-injection boilerplate with no behaviour of its own, so it falls below the granularity of an architectural element. The formatter class itself would be the modelled unit.

Trivial setter on the Pet JPA entity. Accessors are implementation details below the charter's granularity rule. The Pet entity itself would be a data-model object schema, but this method is not an element on its own.

Trivial getter on the Visit entity that returns a field. Accessors are implementation details below model granularity. The Visit entity itself would be a data-model objectschema, and description at most one of its schemaproperty elements, but this method is not an element.

Trivial Formatter.print override that returns a PetType's name or a placeholder. It is a formatting helper below the granularity of an architectural element, with no cross-cutting concern implemented itself.

A trivial toString override on the NamedEntity base class that returns the name or a placeholder. It is a formatting helper and implementation detail, not an architectural element. The callers are test code resolved by name matching and do not indicate any architectural role.

Standard Spring Boot bootstrap boilerplate that only delegates to SpringApplication.run. The PetClinicApplication class is the meaningful application component and entry point; this static main method adds no behaviour of its own and would not be modelled as a separate element.

Spring MVC handler bound to GET /vets.html. A route handler bound to a distinct method and path is an API operation. It drives the server-rendered vet list view: it sets pagination model attributes and redirects when the page number is out of range. Persistence is delegated to findPaginated.

Trivial getter on the Pet entity returning its visits collection. It is an accessor, below the granularity of an architecture element. The Pet entity and its visits relationship would be modelled at the data-model level, not this method.

Handler bound to GET /oups. That makes it an HTTP operation, but it is only a demo endpoint that deliberately throws a RuntimeException to showcase error handling. It carries no business behaviour, so its architectural significance is low. It implements none of the cross-cutting concerns.

This method holds the body of the Pet domain validator. It checks the name is present and within length, the type is set for new pets, and a birth date is present. That is internal application behaviour invoked by the controller's data binding, so it is an application function. It is not a security access control, and it neither persists data nor renders UI.

A trivial setter on the BaseEntity JPA superclass. Accessors are implementation details below the granularity rule. The entity itself would be a data-model object schema, but this method is not an element. It performs no persistence on its own.

Trivial mutator on the Vet entity that adds a Specialty to an internal collection. It is an accessor-level implementation detail of the entity, below the level of an architectural element. It does no persistence I/O itself.

Trivial getter on the Owner entity returning a field value. Accessors are implementation details below the granularity of an architecture element; the telephone field itself would be modelled as a schema property of the Owner object schema, not this method.

A small domain-entity method on the Owner JPA entity that delegates to Pet.addVisit after null checks. It is an in-memory aggregate mutator, an implementation detail of the Owner object schema rather than a standalone architectural element. It performs no direct persistence.

Spring Data repository query method with a JPQL @Query that reads all PetType records ordered by name. It is a named read access pattern against the pet types collection, issued from application code. It is used by the controller and the formatter, so it is a notable but narrow unit.

Protected lazy-initializing accessor on the Vet entity that returns its specialties set. It is a trivial internal helper used only by other Vet methods and is below the granularity of an architectural element. It performs no I/O itself.

Trivial setter on the Pet entity that only assigns a field. Accessors are implementation details below the granularity of an architecture element. The Pet entity itself would be a data-model object schema, but this method is not.

A trivial accessor on BaseEntity that reports whether the id is null. It is an implementation detail of the entity base class, not an architectural element in its own right. It does not itself perform persistence or any other cross-cutting work.

Constructor of VetController that only assigns the injected VetRepository dependency. This is dependency-injection boilerplate and has no behaviour of its own. The controller class may be an element, but this constructor is not one.

Trivial setter on the Visit entity; an accessor is an implementation detail, not an architectural element. The Visit entity itself would be a data-model object schema, but this method only assigns a field and performs no persistence or other cross-cutting work.

Trivial getter on the Pet entity returning its type field. Accessors are implementation details below the granularity of an architectural element. The Pet entity itself would be a data-model object schema, but this method is not an element.

Trivial Spring MVC @ModelAttribute helper returning tomorrow's date for the visit form's minimum date. It is an implementation detail of VisitController with no independent architectural meaning, so it would not be recorded as an element.

A Spring Data repository query method declaring a primary-key read against the owners table. It is a named read access pattern issued by application code, used by several controllers. It is a standard CRUD lookup, so it is notable but not core.

A trivial lazy-initializing accessor on the Vets wrapper DTO, annotated for XML serialization. It is an implementation detail of the data structure rather than an architectural element. The owning Vets class may be modelled, but this getter is not.

Trivial accessor on the NamedEntity base class returning a field value. Accessors are explicitly excluded from being architecture elements under the granularity rule. The owning entity, or its name property, would be modelled in data-model instead. The method implements no cross-cutting concern.

Trivial accessor on BaseEntity that returns the id field. Accessors are implementation details, not architectural elements; the owning entity or its id property would be modelled in data-model, not this getter.
